CLAUDE + OBSIDIAN + LOOP ENGINEERING = KARPATHY'S SECOND BRAIN THAT RUNS ITSELF

the core idea: your Zettelkasten vault is the loop's state, not the chat window

everything Claude knows lives in a .md note, linked to the ones around it

the loop:
> capture - a thought lands in 00-inbox
> context - Claude Opus 5.5 pulls links, tags, and neighbouring notes
> draft - edits happen inside a git worktree, never the live vault
> review - a critic agent checks the diff before anything ships
> commit - appended to the vault, nothing gets rewritten

the key insight: frontmatter fields like supports, contradicts and supersedes are Zettelkasten links the loop can read - the note format is the write API

start with a plain loop, it runs about 2-4x the cost of one direct call

> only move to a full graph once state has to outlive the session, several agents need to coordinate, or you have to explain what changed - that jump runs 10-50x
> if the review step keeps approving its own slop, bolt on Jev engineering: a small decision model gates every ship

one review assistant climbed from 55% to 72% to 84% just by moving through these shapes in order

worth stealing even without a graph: the review step. most vaults skip it, Claude writes straight to live notes

errors compound without a sound for months

set that gate first

OpenAI just released GPT-Live-1.1 for ChatGPT voice today. Here's what you need to know.

GPT-Live-1.1 is an update to OpenAI's GPT-Live voice model, which launched in July 2026. It brings new voices, better accents and less "checking..." to Voice in ChatGPT, Codex and dots. OpenAI says it rolls out today to all users.

The new voices cover French, German, Hindi, Mexican Spanish, Korean and Japanese. OpenAI staff say the update also improves multilingual support overall. One staff member added that there is one surprise voice not listed in the post.

The "checking..." fix targets a common annoyance. Before, the assistant often said things like "let me check that" every few seconds while waiting on updates. Staff describe the new behavior as more natural preambles and more natural delegation. They also say steerability is improved.

The API is not included yet. OpenAI says GPT-Live-1.1 is coming soon to the API. Staff also say the update brings 13 new voices across Chat, Codex and dots.

Users are split. Some praise the better accents and the reduced pauses. Others say the Chinese voice still has a heavy accent. One user asked whether Hindi voices can handle Hinglish, where speakers switch languages mid-sentence. Another is disappointed that Mexican Spanish is the only Spanish accent added.

Users are split. Some praise the better accents and the reduced pauses. Others say the Chinese voice still has a heavy accent. One user asked whether Hindi voices can handle Hinglish, where speakers switch languages mid-sentence. Another is disappointed that Mexican Spanish is the only Spanish accent added.

Key numbers:
- 13 new voices across ChatGPT, Codex and dots
- 6 languages with new voices: French, German, Hindi, Mexican Spanish, Korean, Japanese
- 3 products getting the update: Voice in ChatGPT, Codex, dots
- Original GPT-Live launched July 2026, with API pricing of $0.05 per minute for GPT-Live-1

GPT-Live-1.1 is rolling out now to all users, with API access still to come.
